header.one_liner: Russian Igla-S MANPAD in Indian Army service (48 launchers + 100 missiles, ₹260 cr / €28.9M contract 2023); first batch April 2024, second May 2025; secondary anti-drone role (proven vs Shahed in Ukraine).

what_it_is.prose: The Igla-S (Russian: Игла-С, NATO reporting name SA-24 Grinch) is a Russian man-portable air-defense system (MANPADS) developed by the Konstruktorskoye Byuro Priborostroeniya (KBP) in Tula and exported by Rosoboronexport, both state-owned Rostec subsidiaries. India signed a contract in 2023 for 48 launchers, 100 missiles, night-vision goggles, and a test station for €28.9 million (~₹260 crore). The systems are partly assembled in India at a facility reportedly operated by Astra Microwave and Adani Defence. The first batch of 24 Igla-S launchers was delivered to the Indian Army in April 2024, with a second batch of 24 more launchers delivered in May 2025. The Indian Army's total requirement is reportedly 120 launchers and 400 missiles (per a Vivek Singh X post; not officially confirmed by the MoD). The Igla-S uses infrared homing to engage targets up to 6 km away and at altitudes up to 3.5 km (effective limit 5-7 km). The system has demonstrated anti-drone capability in Ukraine, where Ukrainian brigades have used it to intercept Shahed-136 loitering munitions. The Indian Army is 'recalibrating MANPADS roles' to address low-flying cruise missile and drone threats, expanding the Igla-S beyond its traditional anti-aircraft role.

faq.question: Is the Igla-S an Indian system?
faq.answer: No. The Igla-S (Russian: Игла-С, NATO reporting name SA-24 Grinch) is a Russian man-portable air-defense system (MANPADS) developed by KBP Tula and exported by Rosoboronexport. India contracted 48 launchers + 100 missiles for €28.9M (~₹260 crore) in 2023. The systems are partly assembled in India at a facility reportedly operated by Astra Microwave and Adani Defence, but the design and critical components (especially the infrared seeker) are 100% Russian-origin.

faq.question: Can the Igla-S engage drones?
faq.answer: Yes, in a secondary role. The Igla-S uses infrared homing to engage targets up to 6 km away and at altitudes up to 3.5 km. The system has demonstrated anti-drone capability in Ukraine, where Ukrainian brigades have used it to intercept Shahed-136 loitering munitions. The Indian Army is 'recalibrating MANPADS roles' to address low-flying cruise missile and drone threats, expanding the Igla-S beyond its traditional anti-aircraft role. However, no public confirmation exists of Igla-S being operationally deployed against drones in Indian service.

faq.question: How many Igla-S systems does the Indian Army operate?
faq.answer: India has received 48 launchers and 100 missiles under the 2023 contract — first batch of 24 launchers delivered April 2024, second batch of 24 more launchers delivered May 2025. The Indian Army's total requirement is reportedly 120 launchers and 400 missiles per a Vivek Singh X post, but this figure has not been officially confirmed by the Indian Ministry of Defence.
